name: tariffs and prices
statements: b0
The US Supreme Court ruled that the Trump administration's use of emergency powers to impose tariffs on dozens of countries was unlawful.
b1
As of July 31, 2026, the US government had refunded $100 billion of the tariffs it had collected.
b2
Under the new US-China "30-for-30" framework, each country may import $30 billion worth of non-sensitive goods from the other at reduced tariff rates.
b3
The US manufacturing sector is experiencing a significant expansion with rising orders and job openings across multiple industries.
b4
Escalating US-Canada trade tensions caused job losses in Canada's trade-exposed sectors in August 2026.
b5
Trump's plan to lower tariffs on imported ground beef will not significantly reduce hamburger prices for consumers.
b6
It is unfair that American soybean farmers were left out of the tariff reductions in the new US-China trade agreement.
b7
The United States and China should continue negotiating tariff reductions on goods to stabilize their trade relationship.
b8
President Trump announced that Mesabi Metallics will build a $15 billion steel plant in Iowa.
b9
The Trump administration collected approximately $166 billion in tariff revenues before the Supreme Court struck down the tariff regime.
The US Supreme Court ruled that President Trump exceeded his authority by invoking the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) to impose fentanyl-related and reciprocal tariffs.
The ongoing tariff dispute between the United States and Canada constitutes a trade war.
Trump's 50 percent Section 232 steel tariff contributed to a resurgence in US steel production and investment.
Trump's tariff policy will hurt Republican electoral prospects in the November 2026 midterm elections.
The economic and household costs of Trump's tariffs outweigh whatever political or economic benefits they provide to protected industries.
Republican lawmakers should reassess their support for President Trump's tariff policy given its unpopularity ahead of the November midterms.
Major US retailers and companies including Walmart, Target, and Apple received large tariff refunds following the Supreme Court's ruling.
The average cost of a pound of ground beef in the United States increased nearly 57 percent over a five-year period.
The US Court of International Trade ruled that companies affected by the invalidated tariffs should be refunded.
The tariff refunds represent a financial windfall for major US corporations but not for ordinary consumers.
Tariffs caused many US businesses to raise consumer prices to cover the added costs.
Consumers will receive little or no refund money from businesses that got government tariff refunds.
It is good that the United States is rebuilding its domestic steel manufacturing capacity.
The federal government should continue using tariffs and related incentives to support new domestic steel production projects like the Mesabi Metallics plant in Iowa.
